GPX Routes: The Modern Motorcyclist's Best Friend

GPX (GPS Exchange Format) files have revolutionised motorcycle touring. Instead of memorising routes or fiddling with paper maps, you can load a complete route onto your phone or sat nav and follow it turn-by-turn. Here's everything you need to know about finding, using, and creating GPX routes for UK motorcycle touring.

What Is a GPX File?

A GPX file is a simple data format that stores GPS coordinates as a route, track, or set of waypoints. When loaded into a navigation app, the route appears as a line on the map that you can follow. It's the universal standard for sharing routes between different devices and apps.

How to Use GPX Routes on Your Motorcycle

There are several ways to follow a GPX route while riding:

  • Phone with mount: Load the GPX into an app like OsmAnd, Kurviger, or Calimoto. Mount your phone on the handlebars. This is the cheapest and most flexible option
  • Dedicated sat nav: TomTom Rider and Garmin Zumo series both accept GPX files. More expensive but purpose-built for motorcycle use
  • Apple/Android Auto: Some newer bikes support phone integration. Import GPX into Google Maps or Apple Maps
  • Offline maps: Essential for Highland and rural Welsh touring where signal is patchy. Download map tiles before your trip

Where to Find GPX Routes

VisorUp provides free GPX downloads for all our curated routes — from the NC500 to the Channel Islands Explorer. Other sources include:

  • Wikiloc — Large community of route sharers, filter by motorcycle
  • Kurviger — Motorcycle-specific routing that prioritises curvy roads
  • Calimoto — App with community routes and a curviness rating
  • GPX downloads from touring blogs — Many motorcycle bloggers share their routes as GPX files
Always review a downloaded GPX route on a computer before riding it. Some routes may include impassable tracks, toll roads, or ferry crossings you haven't planned for.

Creating Your Own GPX Routes

The best approach is to use a desktop route planner to create your route, then export as GPX. Recommended tools:

  • VisorUp Route Builder — Our free tool lets you click-to-add waypoints with road-accurate routing and POI markers
  • Kurviger.de — Excellent motorcycle route planner that avoids motorways and maximises curves
  • Google My Maps — Create routes and export as KML (convert to GPX with free online tools)
  • Ride with GPS — Comprehensive route planning with elevation profiles

GPX Tips for UK Touring

When planning GPX routes for the UK, add fuel waypoints in remote areas — especially in the Scottish Highlands and rural Wales where stations can be 50+ miles apart. Include accommodation waypoints so you know when you're approaching your overnight stop. Allow extra distance for B-road detours that your route planner might not suggest. And always carry a paper map as backup — electronics can fail, especially in Scottish rain. Read our How to Use GPX Files for Motorcycle Touring: Complete Guide guide for more. faq.q: What exactly is a GPX file?
faq.a: A GPX, or GPS Exchange Format, file is a simple data format that stores GPS coordinates as a route, track or set of waypoints. When loaded into a navigation app it appears as a line on the map that you follow turn by turn. It is the universal standard for sharing routes between different devices and apps, so a route made on one system works on another.

faq.q: Which apps and devices read GPX files?
faq.a: On a phone, OsmAnd, Kurviger and Calimoto all import GPX and pair with a handlebar mount. For dedicated units, the TomTom Rider and Garmin Zumo series are purpose-built for motorcycle use and accept GPX directly. Some newer bikes support phone integration, letting you import routes into mapping apps. Offline map tiles are essential wherever signal is patchy.

faq.q: Where can I download GPX routes?
faq.a: VisorUp offers free GPX downloads for all its curated routes, from the NC500 to the Channel Islands Explorer. Other good sources include Wikiloc's route-sharing community, Kurviger's curvy-road routing and Calimoto's community routes with a curviness rating. Many touring bloggers also share their favourite routes as GPX files you can load straight onto your device.

faq.q: How do I create my own GPX route?
faq.a: Use a desktop route planner, then export as GPX. The VisorUp Route Builder lets you click to add waypoints with road-accurate routing and POI markers. Kurviger.de avoids motorways and maximises curves, Google My Maps exports as KML for conversion, and Ride with GPS adds elevation profiles. Building on a big screen is far easier than editing on a phone.

faq.q: What should I check before riding a downloaded route?
faq.a: Always review a downloaded GPX on a computer first. Some routes include impassable tracks, toll roads or ferry crossings you have not planned for. For UK touring, add fuel waypoints in remote areas such as the Highlands and rural Wales, where stations can be 50 miles apart, plus accommodation waypoints. Carry a paper map too, as electronics fail in heavy rain.
